title: Translation of source pullbacks and invariance of source-fibre degree
statement: Let $U,R$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme] and let $s,t:R\to U$, $e:U\to R$, $i:R\to R$, and $c:R\times_{s,U,t}R\to R$ form a groupoid scheme [def-a1-groupoid-scheme], with $c(a,b)=a\circ b$. Put $P=R\times_{s,U,t}R$ and $Q=R\times_{s,U,s}R$ [def-pc-fibre-product], both viewed over $R$ by their second projections $p_2,q_2$. There is an isomorphism $F:P\xrightarrow{\sim}Q$ over $R$ given on every test scheme's points by $F(a,b)=(c(a,b),b)$, whose inverse is $G(d,b)=(c(d,i(b)),b)$. In particular $q_2\circ F=p_2$, $G\circ F=\mathrm{id}_P$, and $F\circ G=\mathrm{id}_Q$ as scheme morphisms. No finiteness, flatness, affineness, or relation-monomorphism hypothesis is imposed. If $s$ is finite locally free [def-pc-finite-locally-free], let $d(u)=\dim_{\kappa(u)}\Gamma(R\times_{s,U}\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(u),\mathcal O)$, where $\kappa(u)$ is the residue field [def-weil-residue-field]. Then $d(t(z))=d(s(z))$ for every $z\in R$; equivalently, for every $r\geq0$ the open rank stratum $U_r=\{u:d(u)=r\}$ satisfies $s^{-1}(U_r)=t^{-1}(U_r)$ as open subschemes.

source.place: Tag 02YE (groupoids-lemma-diagram), the two lower cartesian squares, in the absolute groupoid case. Rank consequence: Tag 03BI (groupoids-lemma-finite-locally-free-disjoint-free), comparison of base-changed fibre degrees.

proof.text: Construct the morphisms using the fibre-product universal property [def-pc-fibre-product]. On $P$, $s\circ c=s\circ p_2$ by [def-a1-groupoid-scheme], so the pair $(c,p_2)$ gives $F:P\to Q$. On $Q$, write $q_1,q_2$ for the projections. Since $s q_1=s q_2=t i q_2$, the pair $(q_1,i q_2)$ gives $h:Q\to P$. Also $s c h=s i q_2=t q_2$, so $(c h,q_2)$ gives $G:Q\to P$. The second projections of $F$ and $G$ are respectively $p_2$ and $q_2$. These constructions give exactly the asserted formulas on every test scheme. In Lean, f and g are these explicit pullback lifts, and j is the intermediate lift (q1, i q2).

source.place: Tag 02YE (lemma-diagram), explicit construction for the lower right square; groupoid axioms preceding Tag 0231

proof.text: For any test scheme $H$, associativity, inverse and unit laws [def-a1-groupoid-scheme] give $c(c(a,b),i(b))=c(a,c(b,i(b)))=c(a,e(t(b)))=a$ whenever $s(a)=t(b)$. For a pair with $s(d)=s(b)$ they give $c(c(d,i(b)),b)=c(d,c(i(b),b))=c(d,e(s(b)))=d$. The second coordinate stays $b$ in both computations. Hence the two composites induce identity maps on $H$-points for every $H$. Taking $H=P$ and the point $\mathrm{id}_P$, respectively $H=Q$ and $\mathrm{id}_Q$, proves $G\circ F=\mathrm{id}_P$ and $F\circ G=\mathrm{id}_Q$ as scheme morphisms. Thus $F$ is the claimed isomorphism over $R$, without any geometric hypotheses beyond the groupoid data. A proved private helper groupoid_comp_cancel combines associativity with the right unit law when c(b,d)=e(s(a)); it is applied to (p1,p2,i p2) and (q1,i q2,q2). Pullback extensionality verifies the first-coordinate computations and both second-coordinate equations.

The square (p1,p2;s,t) is the canonical pullback. The projection formulas for the constructed isomorphism F give IsPullback c p2 s s by IsPullback.of_iso_pullback. Under finite local freeness, s is affine, and Scheme.Hom.fiberDegree_of_isPullback (in the module of [def-pc-finite-locally-free]) applied to these two squares gives p2.fiberDegree(z)=s.fiberDegree(t(z)) and p2.fiberDegree(z)=s.fiberDegree(s(z)). Transitivity proves equality of the two fibre degrees. The definition of fiberDegree is definitionally the finrankGamma of fiberToSpecResidueField, so this is precisely the asserted residue-field dimension equality.

source.place: Tag 02YE (lemma-diagram), the two lower squares; Tag 03BI (lemma-finite-locally-free-disjoint-free), comparison over a point z

proof.text: Apply the proved theorem finiteLocallyFree_fiberDimension_isLocallyConstant [lem-weil-pbc-finite-locally-free-degree-locally-constant], which already identifies the locally constant finite-flat rank with the literal fibre dimension. For each natural r, take V to be the open fibre of this locally constant function at r. Its membership equivalence is definitional. Extensionality of opens reduces s inverse V = t inverse V to the fibre-degree equality from the preceding step, point by point. This includes r=0 and empty schemes.

proof_origin.place: Tags 02YE and 03BI. Explicit pullback lifts, cancellation by the groupoid axioms, fibreDegree_of_isPullback, and the existing proved finite-locally-free fibre-dimension local-constancy theorem.

lean.statement: theorem groupoid_source_pullback_translation {U R : Scheme.{u}} (s t : R ⟶ U) (e : U ⟶ R) (i : R ⟶ R) (c : pullback s t ⟶ R) (hG : IsGroupoidScheme s t e i c) : (∃ (F : pullback s t ≅ pullback s s) (h : pullback.fst s s ≫ s = (pullback.snd s s ≫ i) ≫ t), F.hom ≫ pullback.fst s s = c ∧ F.hom ≫ pullback.snd s s = pullback.snd s t ∧ F.inv ≫ pullback.fst s t = pullback.lift (pullback.fst s s) (pullback.snd s s ≫ i) h ≫ c ∧ F.inv ≫ pullback.snd s t = pullback.snd s s) ∧ (s.IsFiniteLocallyFree → (∀ z : R, (s.fiberToSpecResidueField (t z)).finrankΓ = (s.fiberToSpecResidueField (s z)).finrankΓ) ∧ ∀ r : ℕ, ∃ V : U.Opens, (∀ x : U, x ∈ V ↔ (s.fiberToSpecResidueField x).finrankΓ = r) ∧ s ⁻¹ᵁ V = t ⁻¹ᵁ V)
